title: 塞下曲·其二（林暗草惊风）
author: 卢纶
intro: A general shoots at a “tiger” in the dark; at dawn he finds his arrow buried deep in solid rock. Twenty characters retelling a famous Han legend.
analysis: 这首诗化用了汉代名将李广的故事：李广夜里在山中看见草丛里有块石头，以为是老虎，一箭射去，第二天一看，箭头整个射进了石头里。第一句写夜晚的树林黑沉沉的，风一吹草突然乱动——好像有猛兽，气氛一下子紧张起来。第二句只写将军“引弓”，不写射，却让人感到他的镇定和力量。后两句时间跳到第二天天亮：去找那支白羽箭，竟然深深扎在石棱里！诗人不直接说将军多勇猛，而是用结果让读者自己吃惊，这就是“以小见大”。短短二十个字，有声音、有动作、有悬念，像一个微型故事。
analysisEn: This poem retells a legend about Li Guang, a famous Han-dynasty general. Out hunting at night, he saw a rock in the grass, took it for a crouching tiger and shot it. The next morning he found his arrow buried in the stone. The first line sets the mood: the woods are dark, and suddenly the grass thrashes in the wind, as if some beast is moving there. The second line shows only the general drawing his bow — we never see the shot, but we feel his calm and his strength. Then the poem jumps to dawn: they go looking for the white-feathered arrow and find it sunk deep into the edge of a rock. The poet never says “the general was brave and powerful”; he lets the result surprise us and draw the conclusion ourselves. In just twenty characters there is sound, movement, suspense and a twist — a miniature story. Chinese readers know it from childhood, and the phrase 没石饮羽 (“an arrow sunk into stone”) still describes amazing strength.
background: Lu Lun (c. 739–c. 799) was one of the “Ten Talents of the Dali Era” and served for a time on the staff of a frontier commander. His six “Frontier Songs” were written in reply to a general’s poems; this is the second.
pronunciation: 将军 jiāng；没 mò（陷进去，不读 méi）；石棱 léng。机器朗读“没”易读成 méi，已在“朗读用字”列替换同音字。
version: 原题《和张仆射塞下曲六首》，此为第二首。采用通行本。

lines.lit: The woods are dark; the grass is startled by wind;
lines.en: Dark woods — the grass leaps in a sudden wind;

lines.lit: the general at night draws his bow.
lines.en: in the night the general draws his bow.

lines.lit: At dawn they search for the white feathers,
lines.en: At first light they look for the white-feathered arrow —

lines.lit: sunk into the edge of a rock.
lines.en: it is buried deep in the rock.

words.en: to be startled by the wind; a sudden gust
words.note: 现代汉语说“被风吹动”“一阵狂风”。
古义，现代汉语说“天亮”“黎明”。
用箭尾的白羽代指箭，现代汉语直接说“箭”。

words.en: to sink into; to disappear into
words.note: 读 mò，现代汉语“淹没”“埋没”还用。

words.en: the edge or ridge of a rock
words.note: “棱”是物体的边角，现代汉语“棱角”还用。

imagery.name: 草
imagery.zh: 风吹草动，像有猛虎藏在里面，营造夜里紧张的气氛。
imagery.en: Grass thrashing in the wind seems to hide a tiger, building the tension of the night.

imagery.name: 风
imagery.zh: 突然的一阵风制造悬念，也衬出将军临危不乱。
imagery.en: A sudden gust creates suspense — and shows how calm the general stays.
